requirement:
Markdown reports only `Comment` attachments. Each HTML comment block whose
trimmed text starts with `<!--` and ends with `-->` is one attachment.
An inline HTML comment within a paragraph remains paragraph text, and
comment delimiters inside fenced code remain code.
rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test only and did not request implementation source. The test is `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]`, and it carries a `{test}` reference to `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.attachments`. The requirement gives four obligations. The `test.md` case in that test covers each one: - **Only `Comment` attachments.** Each expected markdown attachment is `(Comment, ...)`. The assertion compares the full list of (kind, text) pairs gathered from every item. An extra `Annotation` or any other attachment would fail it. - **Each HTML comment block is one attachment.** The source has a single-line `` and a multi-line ``. The test expects exactly one attachment for each, and the multi-line span is checked as a single attachment. Spans are checked through `source[a.span]`. - **Inline HTML comment stays paragraph text.** The source contains `A word.`, and the expected list does not include it. - **Delimiters inside fenced code stay code.** The source contains a ```` ```html ```` fence holding ``, and the expected list does not include it. The same test also covers two negative boundaries of the "starts with ``" rule: - A non-comment HTML block, `
html
`, is not reported. - An unterminated `` on the same line. The requirement does not name this case, and the unterminated-comment case already covers the "ends with `-->`" boundary. I do not count it as a gap.
